target_customer: Clinical labs, hospitals and patients needing fast infectious disease and antibiotic resistance diagnostics
problem: Slow pathogen identification and antibiotic resistance testing delays correct treatment for infections such as sepsis and gonorrhea.
business_model: clinical laboratory testing service built on nanopore sequencing

founders.name: Fred Turner
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no bio.

competitors.name: Oxford Nanopore Technologies
competitors.what: Maker of the MinION nanopore sequencer, used for rapid pathogen and metagenomic work
competitors.funding_then: Raised about 126 million dollars in December 2016

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable clinical grade nanopore sequencing in under a minute and a CLIA lab operation was research grade work with regulatory hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: The company depended on Oxford Nanopore's technology and a clinical lab certification could be matched by others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced evidence of incumbents copying or buying it; later Target-NG was built on Oxford Nanopore sequencing.

market_need_then: Oxford Nanopore's own resources describe MinION based assays for febrile illness and metagenomic diagnosis of infections, showing a need for faster sequencing diagnostics.

branding.domain_note: shieldbio.com exact .com; it returned 503 when checked in 2026-11.

rebrands.why: Golden says it was formerly known as TL Biolabs; the reason is not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press such as GenomeWeb covered its Target-NG test, but no coverage of the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Shield Bio raised about 12 million dollars from a16z and Refactor and became the first US clinical lab to offer a nanopore based assay, Target-NG for gonorrhea susceptibility. It is now listed out of business by CB Insights and Inactive by YC, but no shutdown post-mortem or closure date was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. Dependence on a third party sequencing platform and a hard regulatory path are context, not sourced causes.
notes: Seed (February 2017, $4.1M, a16z lead) is on Seedtable and StartupIntros and reported by Golden in a search summary; investor lists differ and CB Insights names only Soma Capital. Series A (May 2018, $8M) is on StartupIntros and Seedtable, which labels it seed; I use series_a per StartupIntros and Golden. Totals near 12.1M match. These rest on databases only, no press release. Golden and CB Insights name Sam Parlett as a founder; the YC page lists only Fred Turner, so Parlett is not recorded as a founder. YC team size 28. GenomeWeb article fetch returned 403; its Target-NG claim comes from search snippets. Closure date and cause not public. Only one dated competitor sourced; Illumina listed as incumbent without a dated source.
